summary: A design spec for how the Tutor opens a conversation once a source (a repository now, other document types later) has been read. It describes one arrival event, a Tutor-written opening question with topic rows, a fallback sentence, saving the opening in the chat thread, and the tests that cover it.

options.label: One event for any source
options.what: How a single arrival event carries the kind, summary, options, cannot and run ability, so any source type can use the same call.

options.label: How the Tutor writes the opening
options.what: How a metered server action turns the arrival facts into two or three plain sentences ending in a question, without reading the source itself.

options.label: Opening joins the chat thread
options.what: How the opening and its topic rows become a message, fall back to a fixed sentence on failure, and go grey once a topic is chosen.

options.label: The Run it option and flag
options.what: How a default-off flag adds a Run it row when the source can run.

options.label: Saving and restoring openings
options.what: How each opening is stored as a Tutor entry so a reload brings it back with live rows and no second call.

options.label: What the tests check
options.what: Which tests cover asking once, the fallback, the exact prompt and the flag.

cannot.thing: The actual code behind the mechanism
cannot.why: It names files and functions but shows no code, so behaviour beyond the description cannot be checked here.
No sample opening text or event payload with real values is given.
Only the event shape is built now; Markdown, PDF and slides are mentioned as future.
